items_missed: No 'How are you today?' — she asked for his name twice before he offered anything personal
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' up front — went straight into profile building
Never asked about additional rooms (garage, patio, balcony), storage stops, or additional stops
Never asked about long walks, narrow hallways, or parking/loading access — the destination is a brand-new third-floor apartment build, where access is the most likely surprise

Quote is not accurate for the job described — he deliberately over-quoted at 6.5 hours / $1,468 for a one-bedroom full pack where the customer stated the mattress, couch, and most furniture are being left behind; his own realistic read was closer to 5 hours
Stairs never explained as a time variable despite second-floor stairs-only at origin and third floor at destination
Walk distance never explained as a time variable (only mentioned in the no-extra-fees list)

Save Your Ass prep speech essentially skipped — no 'prep shortens the move / lowers the bill,' no carload tip, no close-out sense-check on prep (consolidation examples granted N/A since Einstein is doing the full pack)
No mention of the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email
Used her name only once, at the open — she used his name five or six times and he never reciprocated
Branch number given only because she asked; hours never stated
top_strength: The insurance explanation was the best in this batch — he contrasted the 60¢/lb state coverage against the $2,000 No Worries plan with a concrete TV example, which is exactly the framing that lands. He also handled a first-time mover with an anxious 'the whole thing' stressor answer by acknowledging it ('we get that all the time') and then walking every fee, the clock, and both quote scenarios until she could repeat them back correctly.
coaching_note: The intentional over-quote is the thing to fix — padding a one-bedroom full pack to 6.5 hours when the furniture is being left behind is exactly the behavior that drags estimate accuracy, and the honest framing he gave it doesn't change the number that gets measured. Quote the realistic five hours, explain the variable that could push it up, and use the Save Your Ass prep speech as the lever instead of the padding.
phone_presence_notes: Real rapport with a nervous first-timer — the Luke/Lucas exchange, the 'better to expect $1,500 and spend $1,000' bit that she echoed back and agreed with, and repeated unprompted thank-yous from her by name.
